message.content: {"caption":"Paired line charts show how the Solve and Propose roles’ reward and token length change over training steps on the abduction task.","description":"The target is a two-panel line chart. Both horizontal axes are Training Steps, marked from 0 to 280 in increments of 40. The legend identifies Solve in purple and Propose in salmon. In the left panel, the vertical axis is Reward, from 0 to about 0.9. Solve rises quickly to around 0.65, fluctuates near 0.5, peaks at about 0.83 around step 190, then drops sharply before fluctuating and ending near 0.38. Propose rises from near zero to around 0.4 by the middle of training, dips to about 0.16 near step 190, then rises with fluctuations to around 0.48 at the end. In the right panel, the vertical axis is Token Length, with a scale extending to above 4,000. Solve stays low through the early steps, rises to roughly 1,500 around steps 120–160, falls back to several hundred, then spikes to nearly 4,000 near step 235, drops, and ends around 3,000. Propose starts around 600–700 tokens, settles mostly in the few-hundred range, briefly dips near step 225, and remains comparatively low through the
